name: Reverse Zero-Width Orders Fill the Complement at Zero Cost
statement: If $(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ is a zero-width order of a nonempty $F\subseteq\{0,1\}^Y$, then, starting from $F^{\mathrm c}$ and adding $f_m,\ldots,f_1$, every addition has step cost zero with the whole initial complement counted as predecessors.
proof: After adding $f_j$, the current class is the complement of the remaining prefix $\{f_1,\ldots,f_{j-1}\}$. Zero-width prefixes are ample, and cube complementation preserves ampleness, so the current class is ample. Its isometry supplies, toward every predecessor, an already present neighbor of $f_j$ whose singleton disagreement lies in the predecessor disagreement; this is exactly the zero-cost condition.
